# `nan-comparison`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports comparison with a NaN value (`std.math.nan`, `std.math.snan`,
`math.nan`, or `math.snan`).
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

In IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic, NaN (Not-a-Number) values never compare
equal to any value, including themselves. Equality comparisons (`==`) always
evaluate to `false`, and inequality comparisons (`!=`) always evaluate to
`true`. Similarly, ordered comparisons (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) always evaluate to
`false`. To test whether a floating-point value is NaN, use `std.math.isNan(x)`.

## When it fires

Whenever comparing a value against a NaN constructor function. For equality and
inequality comparisons, an automatic quickfix rewrites the expression to
`std.math.isNan(x)` or `!std.math.isNan(x)`.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn isMissing(x: f64) bool {
    return x == std.math.nan(f64);
}
```
